claim: FOXA2 binds to the human FLTP promoter in pancreatic progenitors and adult islets.
source: A high amount of the endodermal transcription factor FOXA2 binds the human FLTP promoter in pancreatic progenitors and in adult islets, indicating that FLTP is a direct target of FOXA2 and expressed in these cells.
evidence: The claim is supported by ChIP-seq data shown in Figure 1A and the text description of the figure.

claim: FLTP is a direct target of FOXA2.
source: A high amount of the endodermal transcription factor FOXA2 binds the human FLTP promoter in pancreatic progenitors and in adult islets, indicating that FLTP is a direct target of FOXA2 and expressed in these cells.
evidence: The claim is based on the enrichment of FOXA2 on conserved binding sites in the FLTP promoter region shown in Figure 1A.

claim: The murine Fltp gene consists of six exons.
source: The murine Fltp gene consists of six exons and the spliced mRNA codes for an open-reading frame (ORF) of 567 nucleotides that translates into a protein of 189 amino acids (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the gene structure shown in Figure 1B.

claim: The Fltp spliced mRNA codes for an open-reading frame of 567 nucleotides.
source: The murine Fltp gene consists of six exons and the spliced mRNA codes for an open-reading frame (ORF) of 567 nucleotides that translates into a protein of 189 amino acids (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the mRNA sequence length.

claim: The Fltp ORF translates into a protein of 189 amino acids.
source: The murine Fltp gene consists of six exons and the spliced mRNA codes for an open-reading frame (ORF) of 567 nucleotides that translates into a protein of 189 amino acids (Figure 1B,C).
evidence: This is a direct statement about the protein length.

claim: Fltp protein shows high conservation during evolution.
source: An alignment of the proteins of different species reveals a high conservation during evolution as well as an N-terminal SH3 binding domain and a C-terminal proline-rich repeat (PRR) (Figure 1C).
evidence: The claim is supported by protein alignment data shown in Figure 1C.

claim: Fltp contains an N-terminal SH3 binding domain.

claim: Fltp contains a C-terminal proline-rich repeat (PRR).

claim: The mouse 1700009P17RiK cDNA was identified in a screen for mRNAs highly abundant in ciliated tissues.

claim: Fltp protein localizes to the apical plasma membrane in monociliated mouse node cells.

claim: Fltp protein localizes to the basal body in monociliated mouse node cells.

claim: Fltp mRNA is restricted to the node at E7.5.

claim: Fltp lacZ reporter expression is restricted to the node at E7.5.

claim: Fltp reporter is expressed in the choroid plexi at E11.5.

claim: Fltp reporter is expressed in the prechordal plate at E11.5.
source: E11.5 embryo reveals reporter expression in the choroid plexi (cp), prechordal plate (pcp), eye (e), and floor plate (fp).

claim: Fltp reporter is expressed in the eye at E11.5.
source: E11.5 embryo reveals reporter expression in the choroid plexi (cp), prechordal plate (pcp), eye (e), and floor plate (fp).

claim: Fltp reporter is expressed in the floor plate at E11.5.

claim: Fltp reporter is expressed in the organ of Corti at E17.5.
source: E17.5 IE shows reporter expression in posterior crista ampullaris (pca), lateral crista ampullaris (lca), anterior crista ampullaris (aca), utricular macula (uma), and saccular macula (sma) of the vestibular part as well as in the organ of Corti (oc).

claim: Fltp reporter is expressed in multiciliated lung epithelial cells at E17.5.

claim: Fltp protein is localized at the apical plasma membrane in multiciliated lung epithelial cells.

claim: Fltp protein is localized in cilia of multiciliated lung epithelial cells.

claim: No Fltp immunoreactivity is detected in FltpZV/ZV lungs.
source: No Fltp immunoreactivity is detected in FltpZV/ZV lungs (I and I′).

claim: Fltp homozygous knock-out mice are born at roughly the expected Mendelian ratio.
source: Fltp homozygous knock-out mice are born at roughly the expected Mendelian ratio and are viable and fertile on CD1, C57BL/6NCrl and 129S6/SvEvTac background (Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by breeding data referenced in Figure 1—source data 1.

claim: Fltp homozygous knock-out mice are viable and fertile on CD1, C57BL/6NCrl and 129S6/SvEvTac background.
source: Fltp homozygous knock-out mice are born at roughly the expected Mendelian ratio and are viable and fertile on CD1, C57BL/6NCrl and 129S6/SvEvTac background (Figure 1—source data 1).
evidence: The claim is supported by breeding data referenced in Figure 1—source data 1.

claim: Fltp reporter activity in the inner ear coincides with basal body docking and kinocilium positioning at E13.5.
source: Consistent with a potential function in the PCP pathway, LacZ reporter activity in the IE coincides with BB docking and kinocilium positioning at E13.5 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1E) (McKenzie et al., 2004; Ezan and Montcouquiol, 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by lacZ reporter data and citations to McKenzie et al., 2004 and Ezan and Montcouquiol, 2013.

claim: Fltp reporter activity strongly correlates with the spatial and temporal onset of ciliogenesis in the lung trachea and main bronchi at E14.5–17.5.
source: Furthermore, Fltp reporter activity strongly correlates with the spatial and temporal onset of ciliogenesis in the lung trachea and the main bronchi at E14.5–17.5 (Figure 2E, Figure 2—figure supplement 1G,H).
evidence: The claim is supported by lacZ reporter data shown in Figure 2E and Figure 2—figure supplement 1G,H.

claim: Fltp reporter remains expressed in multiciliated cells of the bronchioles but not in non-ciliated cells of the alveoli at P30.
source: In adult lungs at postnatal day (P) 30, the dual lacZ and H2B-Venus reporter remains expressed in MCCs of the bronchioles, but not in non-ciliated cells of the alveoli (Figure 2—figure supplement 1I,J).
evidence: The claim is supported by reporter expression data shown in Figure 2—figure supplement 1I,J.

claim: Fltp has no function during lung branching morphogenesis.
source: No difference was detectable in FltpT2AiCre/+; R26R/+(Gt[ROSA]26Sor) controls lungs with normal levels of Fltp protein (Soriano, 1999; Lange et al., 2012), FltpZV/+ heterozygous and FltpZV/ZV homozygous mutant lungs, indicating that Fltp has no function during branching morphogenesis (Figure 2E, Figure 3A–C).
evidence: The claim is based on the absence of differences in branching patterns shown in Figure 3A-C.

claim: Fltp knock-out shows a dose-dependent and statistically significant constriction of distal airways.
source: In contrast, measurement and quantification of terminal lung bronchiole diameters revealed a dose-dependent and statistically significant constriction of the distal airways (Figure 3A–D), suggesting that normal Fltp levels are important for lung airway homeostasis.
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative measurements shown in Figure 3A-D.

claim: Normal Fltp levels are important for lung airway homeostasis.
source: In contrast, measurement and quantification of terminal lung bronchiole diameters revealed a dose-dependent and statistically significant constriction of the distal airways (Figure 3A–D), suggesting that normal Fltp levels are important for lung airway homeostasis.
evidence: The claim is inferred from the dose-dependent airway constriction phenotype shown in Figure 3A-D.

claim: Cilia formation is significantly affected in a dose-dependent fashion in Fltp mutant lungs.
source: LSM analysis further confirmed that cilia formation was significantly affected in a dose-dependent fashion (Figure 3E–L), similar to PCP effector knock-down phenotypes in the mucociliary epithelium of Xenopus laevis (Park et al., 2006, 2008).
evidence: The claim is supported by LSM analysis shown in Figure 3E-L.

claim: Fltp-driven H2B-Venus reporter activity is activated at the transition from stage I to stage II when centrosomes/BBs are amplified and docked.
source: In these cultures, Fltp-driven H2B-Venus reporter activity is activated at the transition from stage I to stage II when centrosomes/BBs are amplified and docked in heterozygous and homozygous Fltp ALI cultures (Figure 4B).
evidence: The claim is supported by ALI culture data shown in Figure 4B.

claim: Fltp-H2B-Venus expression increases during maturation until cells are terminally differentiated.
source: Fltp-H2B-Venus expression increases during maturation until cells are terminally differentiated.
evidence: This is a direct statement about reporter expression dynamics.

claim: Fltp is localized to the apical, but not sub-apical actin cytoskeleton.
source: Subcellular co-localization studies further revealed that Fltp is localized to the apical, but not sub-apical actin cytoskeleton and fills the gaps in the actin network from where MT-based cilia project (Figure 4C–Cʹʹʹ,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization studies shown in Figure 4C-C''',E.

claim: Fltp fills the gaps in the actin network from where MT-based cilia project.
source: Subcellular co-localization studies further revealed that Fltp is localized to the apical, but not sub-apical actin cytoskeleton and fills the gaps in the actin network from where MT-based cilia project (Figure 4C–Cʹʹʹ,E).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization studies shown in Figure 4C-C''',E.

claim: Fltp co-localizes with newly synthesized MT plus ends labeled with anti-EB1 antibodies.
source: Moreover, Fltp co-localizes with newly synthesized MT plus ends that are labeled with anti-EB1 antibodies (Figure 4D).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization data shown in Figure 4D.

claim: Fltp localizes directly adjacent to the pericentriolar matrix.
source: Together with the direct adjacent localization of Fltp next to the pericentriolar matrix stained by γ-Tubulin (Figure 4E), these data suggest that Fltp connects BBs and ciliary MT plus ends to the cortical actin cytoskeleton.
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization data shown in Figure 4E.

claim: Fltp+/+ and FltpZV/ZV mTECs differentiate with comparable efficiencies and speed.
source: Fltp+/+ and FltpZV/ZV differentiated with comparable efficiencies and speed as measured by Fltp-driven H2B-GFP expression and centrosome amplification (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), and a comparable number of centrosomes are formed in differentiating Fltp+/+ and FltpZV/ZV mTECs (Figure 4F,G), whereas BB docking and cilia formation was delayed at ALI+2 and +4 days of differentiation (Figure 4F–I, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 1A.

claim: A comparable number of centrosomes are formed in differentiating Fltp+/+ and FltpZV/ZV mTECs.
source: Fltp+/+ and FltpZV/ZV differentiated with comparable efficiencies and speed as measured by Fltp-driven H2B-GFP expression and centrosome amplification (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), and a comparable number of centrosomes are formed in differentiating Fltp+/+ and FltpZV/ZV mTECs (Figure 4F,G), whereas BB docking and cilia formation was delayed at ALI+2 and +4 days of differentiation (Figure 4F–I, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4F,G.

claim: BB docking and cilia formation was delayed at ALI+2 and +4 days of differentiation in FltpZV/ZV mTECs.
source: Fltp+/+ and FltpZV/ZV differentiated with comparable efficiencies and speed as measured by Fltp-driven H2B-GFP expression and centrosome amplification (Figure 4—figure supplement 1A), and a comparable number of centrosomes are formed in differentiating Fltp+/+ and FltpZV/ZV mTECs (Figure 4F,G), whereas BB docking and cilia formation was delayed at ALI+2 and +4 days of differentiation (Figure 4F–I, Figure 4—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: The claim is supported by quantitative analysis shown in Figure 4F-I and Figure 4—figure supplement 1B.

claim: Fltp functions in the process of BB docking and cilia formation.
source: Taken together, these data suggest that Fltp functions in the process of BB docking and cilia formation.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the ALI culture data presented.

claim: The cochlear duct is not significantly shortened or widened in FltpZV/+ and FltpZV/ZV mice at P0.
source: Morphologically the IE looked normal and the cochlear duct is not significantly shortened or widened in FltpZV/+ and FltpZV/ZV mice, indicating that PCP-mediated convergent extension movements are not affected at P0 (data not shown).
evidence: This is a direct statement about morphological analysis.

claim: PCP-mediated convergent extension movements are not affected in Fltp mutants at P0.
source: Morphologically the IE looked normal and the cochlear duct is not significantly shortened or widened in FltpZV/+ and FltpZV/ZV mice, indicating that PCP-mediated convergent extension movements are not affected at P0 (data not shown).
evidence: This is inferred from the normal cochlear duct morphology.

claim: Significant deviations of the polarized arrangement of stereocilia bundles can be seen in IHC and OHC rows in Fltp mutants.
source: However, significant deviations of the polarized arrangement of stereocilia bundles can be seen in IHC and OHC rows with increasing severity closer to the apex along the apico-basal axis (Figure 5B–C,J–N).
evidence: The claim is supported by SEM analysis shown in Figure 5B-C,J-N.

claim: Stereocilia bundle misalignment increases in severity closer to the apex along the apico-basal axis in Fltp mutants.
source: However, significant deviations of the polarized arrangement of stereocilia bundles can be seen in IHC and OHC rows with increasing severity closer to the apex along the apico-basal axis (Figure 5B–C,J–N).

claim: SEM analysis uncovered severe stereocilia bundle morphogenesis defects in Fltp mutants.
source: In addition, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analysis uncovered severe stereocilia bundle morphogenesis defects and mispositioning of the MT-based kinocilium, very similar to phenotypes observed in mutants of spindle positioning proteins, such as Gαi3, mPins, mInsc, and LGN (Figure 5D–I) (Ezan et al., 2013; Tarchini et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by SEM analysis shown in Figure 5D-I.

claim: SEM analysis uncovered mispositioning of the MT-based kinocilium in Fltp mutants.
source: In addition, scanning electron microscopy (SEM) analysis uncovered severe stereocilia bundle morphogenesis defects and mispositioning of the MT-based kinocilium, very similar to phenotypes observed in mutants of spindle positioning proteins, such as Gαi3, mPins, mInsc, and LGN (Figure 5D–I) (Ezan et al., 2013; Tarchini et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by SEM analysis shown in Figure 5D-I.

claim: Fltp mutant phenotypes are similar to phenotypes observed in mutants of spindle positioning proteins Gαi3, mPins, mInsc, and LGN.

evidence: The claim is based on comparison with published phenotypes cited from Ezan et al., 2013 and Tarchini et al., 2013.

claim: FltpZV/ZV; Celsr1crsh/crsh double mutant cochleae revealed an increased degree of misaligned stereocilia bundles compared to Celsr1crsh/crsh single mutants.

claim: FltpZV/ZV; Celsr1crsh/crsh double mutants show an additional fourth OHC row.

claim: Fltp and Celsr1 either act together in the PCP pathway or in two parallel pathways important for cochlea morphogenesis.
source: These data suggest that Fltp and the core PCP gene Celsr1 either act together in the PCP pathway or in two parallel pathways important for the morphogenesis of the cochlea.

claim: No differences in the asymmetric distribution of Vangl1 and Dvl2 at the cell cortex were detected in Fltp+/+ and FltpZV/ZV cochleae at E18.5.
source: No differences in the asymmetric distribution of Vangl1 and Dvl2 at the cell cortex along the medio-lateral axis were detected in Fltp+/+and FltpZV/ZV cochleae at E18.5 (Figure 6F–I), consistent with a function of Fltp downstream of core PCP molecules.
evidence: The claim is supported by immunofluorescence analysis shown in Figure 6F-I.

claim: Fltp functions downstream of core PCP molecules.
source: No differences in the asymmetric distribution of Vangl1 and Dvl2 at the cell cortex along the medio-lateral axis were detected in Fltp+/+and FltpZV/ZV cochleae at E18.5 (Figure 6F–I), consistent with a function of Fltp downstream of core PCP molecules.
evidence: This is inferred from the normal localization of core PCP proteins in Fltp mutants.

claim: Dlg3 specifically localizes in a crescent shape to the bare zone around the BB.
source: Dlg3 specifically localizes in a crescent shape to the bare zone around the BB and co-localizes with the core PCP component Dvl2 at lateral TJs (Figure 7A–Bʹ,G), the area where mPins/LGN, mInsc, and Gαi are localized (Ezan et al., 2013; Tarchini et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by LSM analysis shown in Figure 7A-B',G.

claim: Dlg3 co-localizes with the core PCP component Dvl2 at lateral TJs.
source: Dlg3 specifically localizes in a crescent shape to the bare zone around the BB and co-localizes with the core PCP component Dvl2 at lateral TJs (Figure 7A–Bʹ,G), the area where mPins/LGN, mInsc, and Gαi are localized (Ezan et al., 2013; Tarchini et al., 2013).
evidence: The claim is supported by LSM analysis shown in Figure 7A-B',G.

claim: Dlg3 localizes to the area where mPins/LGN, mInsc, and Gαi are localized.

evidence: The claim is based on comparison with published localization data cited from Ezan et al., 2013 and Tarchini et al., 2013.

claim: Fltp localizes at the interface between Dlg3 and the actin-based stereocilia bundles.
source: Interestingly, Fltp localizes at the interface between Dlg3 and the actin-based stereocilia bundles (Figure 7C–Eʹ), further suggesting that Fltp might be an adaptor protein linking spindle/BB positioning proteins to the apical actin cortex.
evidence: The claim is supported by co-localization data shown in Figure 7C-E'.

claim: The lateral crescent of Dlg3 in Fltp mutants is disturbed.
source: When compared to WT (Figure 8A–Dʹ,J, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A), the lateral crescent of Dlg3 in Fltp mutants is disturbed and BBs are not correctly positioned in the middle of the apical Dlg3 crescent (Figure 8E–Hʹ,J, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A), implicating that Fltp binds to Dlg3 to position BBs, kinocilia, and stereocilia bundles.
evidence: The claim is supported by LSM analysis shown in Figure 8E-H',J and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: BBs are not correctly positioned in the middle of the apical Dlg3 crescent in Fltp mutants.
source: When compared to WT (Figure 8A–Dʹ,J, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A), the lateral crescent of Dlg3 in Fltp mutants is disturbed and BBs are not correctly positioned in the middle of the apical Dlg3 crescent (Figure 8E–Hʹ,J, Figure 8—figure supplement 1A), implicating that Fltp binds to Dlg3 to position BBs, kinocilia, and stereocilia bundles.
evidence: The claim is supported by LSM analysis shown in Figure 8E-H',J and Figure 8—figure supplement 1A.

claim: Fltp physically interacts with Dlg3.
source: We tested this by co-immunoprecipitation experiments of Streptavidin-Flag (SF)-tagged Dlg3 variants and Fltp-myc variants from serum starved and ciliated HEK293T cells (Figure 9A,B). These experiments suggest a physical interaction of Fltp with Dlg3, which requires the highly conserved N-terminal SH3 binding domain of Fltp, but not the SH3 domain of Dlg3 (Figure 9B).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 9A,B.

claim: The physical interaction of Fltp with Dlg3 requires the highly conserved N-terminal SH3 binding domain of Fltp.
source: We tested this by co-immunoprecipitation experiments of Streptavidin-Flag (SF)-tagged Dlg3 variants and Fltp-myc variants from serum starved and ciliated HEK293T cells (Figure 9A,B). These experiments suggest a physical interaction of Fltp with Dlg3, which requires the highly conserved N-terminal SH3 binding domain of Fltp, but not the SH3 domain of Dlg3 (Figure 9B).
evidence: The claim is supported by domain mapping experiments shown in Figure 9B.

claim: The physical interaction of Fltp with Dlg3 does not require the SH3 domain of Dlg3.
source: We tested this by co-immunoprecipitation experiments of Streptavidin-Flag (SF)-tagged Dlg3 variants and Fltp-myc variants from serum starved and ciliated HEK293T cells (Figure 9A,B). These experiments suggest a physical interaction of Fltp with Dlg3, which requires the highly conserved N-terminal SH3 binding domain of Fltp, but not the SH3 domain of Dlg3 (Figure 9B).
evidence: The claim is supported by domain mapping experiments shown in Figure 9B.

claim: Endogenous Dvl2 associates with overexpressed SF full-length Fltp.
source: As Dvl2 localizes directly adjacent to Dlg3 and Fltp in the inner ear, we next examined the association of endogenous Dvl2 and γ-Tubulin with overexpressed SF full-length Fltp and SF-Dlg3 (Figure 9C).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 9C.

claim: Endogenous Dvl2 associates with overexpressed SF-Dlg3.
source: As Dvl2 localizes directly adjacent to Dlg3 and Fltp in the inner ear, we next examined the association of endogenous Dvl2 and γ-Tubulin with overexpressed SF full-length Fltp and SF-Dlg3 (Figure 9C).
evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 9C.

claim: Endogenous γ-Tubulin associates with overexpressed SF full-length Fltp.

claim: Endogenous γ-Tubulin associates with overexpressed SF-Dlg3.

evidence: The claim is supported by co-immunoprecipitation experiments shown in Figure 9C.

claim: Dvl2, Dlg3, Fltp, and γ-Tubulin form a complex during BB transport and positioning.
source: The interaction of Dvl2 with Dlg3 and Fltp and γ-Tubulin with Dvl2 and Dlg3 suggests that these proteins form a complex during BB transport and positioning.

claim: Dlg3 is required for BB positioning in the inner ear.

evidence: The claim is supported by knock-out analysis shown in Figure 8K,L and Figure 8—figure supplement 1B,C.

claim: Dlg3 is a BB positioning protein that is anchored at apical TJs.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that Dlg3 is a BB positioning protein that is anchored at apical TJs (Van Campenhout et al., 2011) and cooperates with Fltp to position BB at the apical cortex of HCs in the cochlea at E18.5.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the localization and functional data, with citation to Van Campenhout et al., 2011.

claim: Dlg3 cooperates with Fltp to position BB at the apical cortex of HCs in the cochlea at E18.5.
source: Taken together, these results suggest that Dlg3 is a BB positioning protein that is anchored at apical TJs (Van Campenhout et al., 2011) and cooperates with Fltp to position BB at the apical cortex of HCs in the cochlea at E18.5.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the genetic and biochemical interaction data.

claim: Fltp is a potential PCP effector regulating the cytoskeleton.
source: Several lines of evidence suggest that Fltp is a potential PCP effector regulating the cytoskeleton.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on multiple lines of evidence presented in the study.

claim: Fltp is expressed in several tissues known to depend on active PCP signalling.
source: First, the Fltp gene and reporter are expressed in several tissues known to depend on active PCP signalling, such as the node, ependymal cells, floor plate, lung, eye, and IE.
evidence: This is based on the expression analysis presented in Figure 2 and supplementary figures.

claim: Fltp expression kinetic correlates with dynamic PCP acquisition, terminal differentiation, and cellular morphogenesis in the lung and the IE.
source: Second, Fltp expression kinetic correlates with dynamic PCP acquisition, terminal differentiation, and cellular morphogenesis in the lung and the IE.
evidence: This is based on the temporal expression analysis presented in the study.

claim: Fltp is not required for PCP establishment.
source: If this is the case, then Fltp seems to be a downstream effector molecule in the PCP pathway, as it is not required for PCP establishment, but rather for cell intrinsic PCP transduction leading to cytoskeletal rearrangements.
evidence: This is based on the normal localization of core PCP proteins in Fltp mutants shown in Figure 6F-I.

claim: Fltp is required for cell intrinsic PCP transduction leading to cytoskeletal rearrangements.
source: If this is the case, then Fltp seems to be a downstream effector molecule in the PCP pathway, as it is not required for PCP establishment, but rather for cell intrinsic PCP transduction leading to cytoskeletal rearrangements.
evidence: This is inferred from the phenotypes observed in Fltp mutants.

claim: Phenotypes observed for the PCP effectors Intu and Fuz in the mucociliary epithelium of the frog and Fltp in the murine lung are strikingly similar.
source: This is supported by the fact that phenotypes observed for the PCP effectors Intu and Fuz in the mucociliary epithelium of the frog and Fltp in the murine lung are strikingly similar (Park et al., 2006, 2008).
evidence: This is based on comparison with published phenotypes cited from Park et al., 2006, 2008.

claim: Fltp cooperates with Dlg and Dvl family members to regulate apical BB transport and docking of BBs in multiciliated tissues.
